newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer, eyes on Tokyo Bay oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer, eyes on Tokyo Bay oil spill.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices went higher in slow afternoon trade on Wednesday, with traders carefully watching the development of an oil spill in Tokyo Bay, market participants said.

"I haven't seen any actual impact of the accident on the (naphtha) market yet, but I can't take my eye off the spill with many major petrochemical firms located around the bay," one naphtha trader said.
A supertanker carrying 257,000 tonnes of crude oil leaked an estimated 13,400 tonnes of its cargo after hitting a reef in the bay on Wednesday morning.

Petrochemical manufacturers with their plants around Tokyo Bay, including Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, Maruzen Petrochemical Co Ltd and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd, said their operations have not been affected by the spill.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half September was assessed at about $201.00/$202.00 per tonne, compared with Tuesday's $199.25/200.50.
Second-half September was quoted about 50 cents higher than the first half of the month.
On Tuesday, one second-half September contract was traded at $201.00, traders said. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
